channel.title: Sashank Silwal's Blog
channel.description: Blog posts on machine learning, computer science, and software engineering by Sashank Silwal.

item.title: I Asked GPT-6 Astra for a 3D Boudhanath and Got 2,004 Prayer Flags
item.description: I've used Claude daily for months. Then GPT-6 Astra landed, so I pointed it at a 3D reconstruction of Boudhanath. Two hours later, I hadn't written a line.

item.title: Claude Code Features I Found by Using It Every Day
item.description: I've used Claude Code daily for months. The biggest wins came from features I stumbled onto, not the docs: rewind, queued prompts, /goal, /powerup, and more.

item.title: Docker Basics: What a Dead Server Taught Me About Containers
item.description: I spent a week setting up a Fortran weather model on a server. Then it died. Here's the Docker intro and tips I wish I'd had before redoing it all by hand.

item.title: When Invariant Learning Helps a GNN Recommender (and When It Collapses)
item.description: LightGCN's Recall@20 drops 46% when you swap a random split for a temporal one. Here's how invariant learning partially fixes it, and the failure mode we found when IRM is pushed too hard.

item.title: Why Deep GNNs Don't Work: Oversmoothing, Oversquashing, and Underreaching
item.description: Stacking layers works for CNNs and Transformers. Try it on a graph neural network and it breaks in three distinct ways, each with its own mechanism and its own fix.

item.title: Should You Even Use a GNN?
item.description: Most graph-shaped problems aren't graph problems. A framework for deciding when a GNN is worth the complexity, and when XGBoost with aggregate features will quietly beat it.

item.title: 15 Claude Code Features Most People Don't Know About
item.description: Boris Cherny from Anthropic shared his favorite hidden features: mobile coding, session teleporting, automated loops, parallel worktree agents, voice input, and more.

item.title: Domain Adaptation: Why Your Model Breaks When the Background Changes
item.description: Car classifiers that fail in garages, X-ray models that break across hospitals, and how MMD forces neural networks to learn features that transfer across domains.

item.title: Sharp vs. Flat Minima: Why Some Models Generalize and Others Just Memorize
item.description: Neural networks can memorize random labels. So why do they generalize on real data? The answer is in the geometry of the loss surface.

item.title: Invariance and Equivariance: Teaching Neural Networks About Symmetry
item.description: Why CNNs break when you rotate the input, how the Reynolds operator builds symmetry into weight space, and a 1,800-parameter network that crushed a 454,000-parameter CNN.

item.title: Disentangled Representations: Why VAEs Can't Disentangle (and What Actually Works)
item.description: Locatello et al. proved unsupervised disentanglement is impossible. Here's why rotational symmetry breaks identifiability, and how sparsity fixes it.

item.title: Why Your Model Works in the Notebook but Breaks in Production
item.description: Covariate shift, concept drift, retraining strategies, and the monitoring that keeps ML systems alive after deployment.

item.title: Recommendation Systems: From Matrix Factorization to Two-Tower Models
item.description: Collaborative filtering, content-based methods, two-tower retrieval, GNN-based recs, and the popularity bias problem that breaks most systems.

item.title: Airflow and DAGs: The Orchestration Tool Every Data Team Ends Up Using
item.description: What Airflow is, how DAGs work, building your first ML pipeline, error handling, and when to use something else instead.

item.title: Spark, Hadoop, and PySpark: When You Actually Need Distributed Computing
item.description: Hadoop's legacy, why Spark replaced it, PySpark for ML feature engineering, and the honest threshold for when single-machine tools stop working.

item.title: Deploying ML Models with SageMaker: Endpoints, Scaling, and When Not to Bother
item.description: Real-time and serverless endpoints, auto-scaling, A/B testing with production variants, cost optimization, and when a FastAPI server is the better choice.

item.title: Getting Started with Claude Code: Everything I Wish I Knew on Day One
item.description: A beginner's guide to Claude Code covering CLAUDE.md, context management, key commands, and the feedback loop that makes it actually useful.

item.title: Claude Code Beyond the Basics: Agents, Context Engineering, and Production Workflows
item.description: An intermediate guide to Claude Code covering context management, CLAUDE.md patterns, subagents, custom commands, hooks, MCP, skills, and CI integration.

item.title: Building a RAG System from Scratch
item.description: A step-by-step guide to building retrieval-augmented generation with Python. Embeddings, vector search, and generation, no frameworks required.

item.title: Context Poisoning: How Attackers Manipulate LLM Context Windows
item.description: Prompt injection, data poisoning in RAG systems, and adversarial inputs that hijack LLM behavior. Real attack vectors and practical defenses for production systems.

item.title: What is Fine-Tuning, and Why Does Every AI Company Do It?
item.description: RLHF, LoRA, full fine-tuning explained without the jargon. How companies take a base model and turn it into something actually useful.

item.title: Fitting Big Models on Small GPUs
item.description: Quantization techniques (GPTQ, GGUF, AWQ), distillation as a size reduction strategy, and practical tradeoffs for running 70B models on consumer hardware.

item.title: Model Distillation: The Technique, The Controversy, and How To Do It
item.description: What model distillation is, how DeepSeek allegedly used it on frontier model outputs, and a practical guide with lessons from our reasoning distillation paper.

item.title: Automated Rule Generation for Fraud Detection Using Deep Learning and Explainability
item.description: How to automatically extract interpretable, auditable fraud detection rules from LSTM models using SHAP, Anchors, knowledge distillation, and temporal pattern mining.

item.title: UrbanTherm: GPU-Accelerated Surface Energy Balance for Urban Microclimate Modeling
item.description: How we extended SOLWEIG with a full surface energy balance solver, Newton-Raphson surface temperatures, multi-layer conduction, canopy transpiration, and spatial air temperature, all running on GPU at 1m resolution.

item.title: Industry-Level RAG Practices: A Comprehensive Reference
item.description: A detailed guide covering the full RAG pipeline: chunking, embeddings, vector databases, retrieval strategies, reranking, advanced architectures (CRAG, Self-RAG, Graph RAG, RAPTOR), evaluation, and production deployment.
